The chain, top to bottom; a problem is the first link that is down:

```text
DCS (mission and hooks environments)
  └─ bridge DLL + Lua layer    loaded by one line in <DCS>\Scripts\MissionScripting.lua
                               and by Saved Games\DCS\Scripts\Hooks\sortie-hook.lua
       └─ link (named pipe) ─► sortied (gRPC 127.0.0.1:50777)
                                 ◄─ your logic binary (Logic.Attach)
                                 ◄─ sortie-gen (register, launch, watch, results)
                                 ◄─ sortie CLI (status, events, top)
```

The Saved Games folder is `%USERPROFILE%\Saved Games\DCS` (a dedicated server started with
`-w DCS.server`: `DCS.server`, and every command gets `--instance server`).

## Setup on a machine with DCS

1. Unzip `sortie-runtime-0.4.0-win64.zip` from the GitHub release of
   `lynxr/sortie-sdk` and follow its README; check it against `SHA256SUMS`.
2. `sortie.exe install` from a console **run as administrator**: it copies the Lua layer, the
   hook and the bridge DLL into Saved Games, creates `Sortie\link.secret` and
   `Sortie\tokens.toml`, and adds one line to `<DCS>\Scripts\MissionScripting.lua` (the only
   change in the DCS folder). `--dry-run` shows the plan; `--no-patch` leaves
   `MissionScripting.lua` alone; `--dcs <folder>` picks the install.
3. **Restart DCS itself** (not only the mission). The hooks part of the layer and a new bridge
   DLL load only when DCS starts.
4. `sortie.exe doctor`: done when it exits 0. `doctor --fix` (administrator) restores the
   `MissionScripting.lua` line after a DCS update overwrote it.
5. `sortied.exe --dev`: local API calls need no token; spawns and destroys need `.key()`. Keep
   the console open: it logs every attach and refusal. DCS and `sortied` start in any order.
6. Register the mission (`uv run python scenario.py register`), start the logic
   (`cargo run --release -- --dev`), then fly: open
   `Saved Games\DCS\Missions\Sortie\<scenario>-<build_id>.miz` (single player) or
   `scenario.py launch` (dedicated server).
7. Done when `sortie status` shows `session <id> (<scenario>)` with `1 logic client(s)` and the
   logic's stderr says `session started`.

## Where to look

| Source | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| the DCS screen | `Sortie bridge is not installed: run sortie doctor` (the mission found no bridge); `Sortie: <reason>` (the engine refused the mission) |
| `sortie status` | engine and bridge versions, DCS version, `link hooks/mission: up/down`, the session, model time, `PAUSED`, logic clients, `note` lines with the reason something is degraded; since 0.4.0 the mission link's `events copied (N DCS calls, T ms; at most N us between two pumps)` and `snapshots read N objects` (what the Lua layer's copies cost inside DCS) |
| `sortie events --kind dead --limit 20`, `scenario.py watch` | the live event stream |
| `sortie top` | health, links, credits, queues, refreshed every second; `ev<N>us` on the mission link: the longest event copy between two pumps (0.4.0) |
| `Saved Games\DCS\Logs\dcs.log` | Lua layer lines start with `Sortie:` (mission) or come from the `SORTIE` subsystem (hooks): link up/down, boot errors. `Select-String Sortie dcs.log` |
| `Saved Games\DCS\Logs\sortie-bridge.log` | the bridge DLL |
| `Saved Games\DCS\Sortie\Logs\sortied.log.*` | the engine (also on its console), including the `doctor` checks it runs at start |
| the logic's stderr | attach, `session started` / `session ended`, every recorded error with its Rust call site; `SORTIE_LOG=debug` for more |
| `scenario.py results` | the outcome, fates, kills, flags and report of the last session |

## The development loop

- **Logic change:** stop the logic (Ctrl-C), `cargo build --release`, start it again. The
  running session continues; the mission function starts with `Start::AfterCrash` and replays:
  keyed commands, `once` and named timers do not repeat. (`sortie dev` with hot reload is not
  available yet.)
- **Scenario change without new symbols** (positions, units, weather): `register` a new
  build and load it. A new build is a new turn: `Start::Fresh`.
- **New or renamed symbols:** `lock`, rebuild the logic, `register`, load the new build. An
  old logic is refused by a mission that lacks its symbols.
- **Same build again:** `scenario.py restart` (multiplayer host or server), or load the same
  `.miz` again in single player: `Start::Restart`, the world is back to the manifest.
- Only one logic per scenario can be attached: stop the old process before starting a new
  one.

## Facts that cause most surprises

- **Restart DCS after `sortie install`.** A new DLL is named in `Scripts\Sortie\pending.txt`
  and becomes active at the next DCS start; the hooks Lua loads only at DCS start. A stale
  layer shows as a `sortie status` note: "the Lua layer DCS loaded differs from what
  `sortie install` put there ...: run `sortie install` again and restart DCS itself".
- **Multiplayer slots and airfields.** DCS offers a parking slot only to the coalition that
  owns the airfield. A player who stays a spectator after picking a slot: the airfield belongs
  to someone else. `player_flight` handles it; a client group added in a `@sc.pydcs` hook needs
  its airfield owner set in the hook (the build warns).
- **Unit ids are strings in DCS 2.9.31.** `Unit:getID()` returns a string there. The Lua layer
  and the engine of this runtime accept both forms; in the SDK `Entity.unit_id` is a number,
  and so are the id reads of `ctx.dcs()` (`static_object(o).id()`, `airbase(a).id()`).
  A world that stays empty (no units in `wait_until`, nothing in `sortie events`) with an older
  runtime: install this one and restart DCS.
- **Mission Editor round trips are safe** for a built `.miz` (open, re-save, fly from the
  editor): the bootstrap is an inline DO SCRIPT. The `dcs.log` error
  `[string "DictKey_..."]:1: '=' expected near '<eof>'` means a DO SCRIPT in the dictionary
  form: the `.miz` went through a pydcs load and save, or a hook used pydcs's `DoScript`
  instead of `sortie_gen.miz.InlineDoScript`. Groups, units and zones edited in the editor no
  longer match the manifest: edit `scenario.py`.
- **Pause stops model time.** Commands to the mission wait while DCS is paused (unless sent
  with `.on_pause(Fail)`), `ctx.sleep` and timers stop, and the type check of `register` cannot
  run.
- **Measurements of DCS itself** (event ids, timer cadence, sampling cost) are not part of SDK
  0.4.0: `sortie probe` prints "`sortie probe` lands in M0" and exits with code 2;
  `sortie dev`, `sortie trace` and `sortie record` are not built yet either (M4). Report what
  you measure with the DCS version, FPS and hardware.

Failure signatures and fixes, symptom first: [references/failures.md](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-live-debugging/references/failures.md).
Mission-side errors (`sortie::*` codes): the sortie-mission-logic skill,
`references/errors.md`. Docs (Russian): https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/.

<!-- source: agents/sortie-live-debugging/references/failures.md -->

# Failure signatures (for agents)

Symptom first. Check the links of the chain in this order: DCS screen and `dcs.log`, then
`sortie status`, then the `sortied` console, then the logic's stderr.

## The mission does not attach

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| screen: `Sortie bridge is not installed: run sortie doctor` | the mission found no `SORTIE` global: the `MissionScripting.lua` line is missing (a DCS update rewrites the file) or the Lua boot failed | `sortie doctor`; `sortie doctor --fix` as administrator; then read the `Sortie:` error in `dcs.log` |
| `dcs.log`: ``Sortie: lfs/io/package are not available: the Sortie line must come before the sanitizer in MissionScripting.lua (run `sortie doctor --fix`)`` | the line sits after the sanitizer | `sortie doctor --fix` as administrator |
| `dcs.log`: ``Sortie: Scripts/Sortie/active.txt is missing: run `sortie install` `` | no bridge installed in this Saved Games folder (or another instance) | `sortie install` with the right `--instance`, restart DCS |
| screen: ``Sortie: build <id> (<scenario>) is not registered with this engine; register it with `sortie-gen register` ...`` | the `.miz` came from an offline `build`, or the engine's database is another one (`--db memory` forgets on restart) | `scenario.py register` and open the registered copy from `Missions\Sortie`, or start `sortied --manifest dist\<id>.manifest.pb` |
| screen: `Sortie: the mission's digest ... does not match build ...` | the `.miz` was changed after the build or belongs to another build | build and register again; edit `scenario.py`, not the `.miz` |
| screen: `Sortie: the mission says scenario ...` / `... schema ...` | the bootstrap and the registered build disagree | rebuild and register |
| nothing on screen; `sortie status`: `link mission: down`, note `no mission link: no Sortie mission is running` | `sortied` is not running, the mission has not started, or the link points elsewhere | start `sortied`; same `--instance` for `install`, `doctor` and `sortied`; `dcs.log`: `mission link down: <error>; retrying` names the reason |
| note `the DCS hooks link is not connected (is DCS running with Scripts/Hooks/sortie-hook.lua?)` | DCS was not restarted after the install, or the hook is missing | restart DCS; `sortie doctor` checks `hook` |
| note ``the Lua layer DCS loaded differs from what `sortie install` put there (...): run `sortie install` again and restart DCS itself`` | an update of the layer while DCS ran | as it says (for the mission part: restart the mission) |
| `dcs.log`: ``[string "DictKey_..."]:1: '=' expected near '<eof>'`` | a DO SCRIPT in pydcs's dictionary form | rebuild from `scenario.py`; hooks use `sortie_gen.miz.InlineDoScript`; never load/save a built `.miz` with pydcs |

## The logic does not run

| Symptom (logic stderr) | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ``cannot reach the engine at http://127.0.0.1:50777: ... (is `sortied` running?); retrying in N s`` | no engine at that address | start `sortied`; `--engine` / `SORTIE_ENGINE` |
| `attaching`, then nothing | no session of this scenario runs yet; the logic waits for one | start the mission; the scenario name of the logic and the mission must match |
| ``error[sortie::transport]: Logic.Attach at ... failed: ... (set SORTIE_TOKEN to a token with the `logic` role)``, exit code 2 | `sortied` without `--dev` needs a token | `SORTIE_TOKEN` from `Saved Games\DCS\Sortie\tokens.toml` (role `logic`), or `sortied --dev` on your own machine |
| ``error[sortie::rejected]: the engine rejected this logic: logic `x` was built against a different `s` schema: N symbol(s) missing from the running mission``, exit code 2 | the mission in DCS lacks symbols the logic was built with | build the logic and the mission from the same `scenario.lock.json`; `register` and load the new build |
| ``another PRIMARY logic is attached for `s` `` | a second copy of the logic | stop the old process |
| `the engine shut this logic down`, exit code 0 | the engine stopped, or the logic stopped reading (a blocked thread: 4096 unread messages) | restart it; remove the blocking code |
| `session started` with `kind=AfterCrash` after a restart of the logic | expected: same session, the mission function replays | nothing; keys, `once` and timers keep it from repeating |

## The mission runs, but wrong

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a player picks a slot and stays a spectator (multiplayer) | the airfield belongs to another coalition | `player_flight` sets the owner; for a client group from a hook, set the airfield's coalition in the hook; read the build warnings |
| `sortie status` shows the session, but `wait_until` on units never fires and `sortie events` stays silent | the world stays empty: an older runtime reads DCS 2.9.31's string unit ids as numbers | install the current runtime, restart DCS |
| `sortie::invalid`: spawn or destroy without a key | `sortied --dev` or the logic's `--dev` | `.key("step-name")` |
| a spawn twice after a logic restart | the spawn had no key, or its key changes between runs | a stable key per step |
| `sortied`: `an event's time is far ahead of model time: it moves no clock`; `sortie status`: `N event times far ahead of model time ignored` | an event came with another clock than model time: an F10 mark's time of day from a Lua layer older than 0.4.0, or time acceleration in single player. The engine's clock is not affected (before 0.4.0 such a mark froze ticks and timers) | `sortie install` and restart the mission; nothing under time acceleration |
| `ctx.destroy` of a static, or `spawn_static` with `Replace`, → `sortie::lua_error`: ``DCS did not remove the static `X`: it still exists 10 pumps after destroy()`` | DCS kept the object (reported for FARPs; not measured); the world keeps the static and its airbase alive | do not plan on removing a FARP; give the new static another name, or leave the old one |
| `sortie::timeout` on spawns, note `N command(s) waiting: spawn rate limit (2 groups / 24 units per second)` | too many spawns at once | spawn in a loop, cap the count, raise `.timeout(..)` |
| `sortie::timeout`: "the deadline passed before the command could start (tasking delay after spawn (2 frames and 0.5 s))", and the mission function stopped there | a `set_task` / `set_option` right after a spawn waited for the delay until its deadline and never reached DCS (`e.limit()`: `TaskingDelay`); with 0.3.0 an F10 mark froze the clock the delay counts on | engine 0.4.0 (the clock and the hold are fixed); key the command, retry it once on `Timeout` and log the rest instead of returning it with `?` |
| `sortie::timeout`: "`op` was sent to DCS but no result arrived before the deadline" | DCS did not answer in time; the command may still run (`e.limit()` is `None`) | retry only with the same `.key(..)` (it joins the late result); check `sortie top` for a busy pump |
| `sortie::invalid`: "key `k` was already used for a different command in session ..." | the command under that key changed (a new heading, target or option), also after a logic restart | a new key for the changed command (`k-v2`) |
| `sortied` does not start: ``engine.toml [calls]: `Controller.setOption`: `enum:..`: an enum table is 2 to 6 Lua names from one of the enum roots (AI, Airbase, ...)`` | an owner entry names an enum table of 7 names, from a data root (`env`, `net`, `DCS`, `timer`, `Warehouse`) or, in a hooks entry, a DCS table; 0.3.0 refused even 5 names | name the published table's whole path from an enum root (`enum:AI.Option.Ground.val.ALARM_STATE`), or declare the argument `number` |
| every unit of a spawned ground group faces the same heading (Tacview yaw), the template's offsets between them lost | `.at(point, heading)` gives every unit that one heading and does not turn the formation (0.1.0 to 0.4.0) | `.at_formation(point, heading)` (API revision 3) under a new key; the template's reference heading is `Template.heading_rad`, else its first unit's |
| `sortie::rejected`: "rate limit: the heavy calls of (writer) cost more than 20 ms of DCS time per second (dcs_time.heavy ...); the next one may go in N s" | a heavy call (a long road path) took more DCS time than the writer's heavy budget holds (200 ms, refilled 20 ms a second); reads are not held | wait the N s before the next heavy call; ask a road path once per route; ends further apart cost more (at most 300 km) |
| `sortie::rejected`: "rate limit: the reads of (writer) cost more than 20 ms of DCS time per second" | a read or a batch (any batch, a mutate in it too) cost more DCS time than the read budget; since 0.4.0 a single read waits at most 1 s, a batch until the whole debt is paid back | retry after `e.retry_after()`; split big batches and spread them; a costly read belongs to class heavy |
| `sortie::rejected`: "rate limit: the previous heavy call of (writer) has not come back yet ..." (`DcsTime`, `dcs_time.heavy`, no `retry_after()`) | a heavy call sent while the logic's previous heavy call is still queued, running or awaited after a `Timeout` (0.4.0: one at a time per writer) | send the next heavy call after the previous one answered, not two at once |
| a command `.after(a)` fails at once with `a`'s code (`Rejected`, `Invalid` ...) and `e.limit()` `After` | `a` failed; the command never ran, and sent again it fails the same way | send `a` again, then this command `.after(..)` the new one |
| `sortie::rejected`: "rate limit: (writer) may make 200 read calls per second" | the read count: a batch is charged every call, so a 256-read batch leaves the next one 1.28 s to wait | `e.limit()` (`CallRate`, `call_rate.read`) and `e.retry_after()` name it: wait that long, or send smaller batches spread over time |
| commands hang, `sortie status` says `PAUSED` | DCS is paused: mission commands wait | unpause, or `.on_pause(v1::PausePolicy::Fail)` |
| `ctx.group(groups::X)` → `sortie::not_in_world` | late activation or the group is dead | spawn it from a template instead; check `alive_count()` |
| `ctx.group(groups::X)` → `sortie::unknown_symbol` | the mission in DCS was built from another lock | rebuild both sides from one lock |
| `register` stops: `DCS on the server does not know N type(s) ...` | a misspelled type or a module or mod missing on the server | fix the type or install it there; `--no-validate` skips |
| `register` warns `unit and static types not checked: ...` | no mission ran in DCS, or it was paused | run the lobby (`sortie-gen lobby`) unpaused |
| `scenario.py restart` → `FAILED_PRECONDITION`: `Missions.Restart needs DCS running as a multiplayer server ...` | single player | restart from the DCS menu, or host in multiplayer |
| `restart` → `DCS did not say whether it runs multiplayer: the Sortie hooks layer DCS loaded predates ...` | DCS was not restarted after `sortie install` | restart DCS itself |
| `scenario.py launch` fails on a single-player DCS | `launch` loads missions through the server API | open the registered `.miz` yourself |

## `sortie doctor` checks

| Check | When it fails | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dcs install`, `saved games`, `writedir` | wrong folder or instance | `--dcs <DCS World folder>`, `--instance <name>`, `--saved-games <folder>` |
| `MissionScripting`, `sanitizer` | the line is missing, misplaced, or the sanitizer was changed | `sortie doctor --fix` as administrator; restore the stock sanitizer |
| `hook`, `lua layer`, `bridge dll` | files missing or changed | `sortie install`, then restart DCS |
| `lua.dll` | this DCS build changed `lua.dll`: the bridge does not match it | a runtime release built for this DCS version is needed: report it |
| `link secret`, `api tokens` | not created yet | `sortie install` |
| `missionList` | an empty mission list on a dedicated server (the server does not start) | add a mission, e.g. a `sortie-gen lobby` mission |
| `unsafe api` (warning) | `autoexec.cfg` opens `net.allow_unsafe_api` to missions | Sortie does not need it |

<!-- source: agents/sortie-mission-logic/SKILL.md -->

Skill `sortie-mission-logic` (sortie-mission-logic/SKILL.md): Sortie mission logic in Rust (crate `sortie`, DCS World). Use when writing or changing a `#[sortie::mission]` or code that uses `Ctx` (commands, `.key()`, `ctx.once`, waits, events, F10 menus, flags, state, timers, `end_session`), when handling `Start` kinds, when a `sortie::*` error code appears (`sortie::gone`, `sortie::invalid`, `sortie::unknown_symbol`, ...), or when designing a long multiplayer mission. Applies to any crate that depends on `sortie` or calls `sortie::include_scenario!`.


# Sortie mission logic

The mission logic is an ordinary async Rust program next to DCS. The engine `sortied` owns
the link to DCS; the logic attaches to it over gRPC and gets one call of its mission function
per session.

- **Reads are local and synchronous.** `ctx.world()` is a replica of the DCS world, updated
  10 times a second and by every event. No RPC.
- **Writes are commands.** Every write is a `Cmd` builder; `.await` sends it and resolves when
  DCS has executed it (or with a `sortie::Error`).
- **The mission function is a replayable script.** It runs again from the top when the logic
  process restarts inside a running session (`Start::AfterCrash`). Every step must be safe to
  run twice: keyed commands, `ctx.once`, named timers, waits on world state.
- **One thread.** `Ctx` is cheap to clone and not `Send`; background work is `ctx.spawn`.
- **Typed scenario.** `groups::X`, `zones::X`, `templates::X`, `flags::X`, `airbases::X`,
  `menus::X` come from the scenario lock; a symbol of another scenario does not compile.
- **All game logic is here.** The `.miz` holds the map side only; what happens in the
  mission is this Rust code, never a DO SCRIPT in the `.miz` (rule 1).

## Project layout

A mission repository starts as a copy of the SDK's `template/` folder:

```text
my-mission/
  Cargo.toml             # the logic crate (package my_mission_logic)
  build.rs               # turns the lock into typed symbols
  src/lib.rs             # include_scenario! and the #[sortie::mission]
  src/main.rs            # one line: sortie::main!(my_mission_logic::run);
  scenario.py            # the scenario (sortie-gen); see the sortie-scenario skill
  scenario.lock.json     # written by `python scenario.py lock`; commit it, never edit it
  pyproject.toml         # uv project with the sortie-gen dependency
```

`examples/op_north` keeps the crate in a `logic/` subfolder instead; both work.

```toml
# Cargo.toml
[package]
name = "my_mission_logic"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.89"

[dependencies]
sortie = { git = "https://github.com/lynxr/sortie-sdk", tag = "v0.4.0" }
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }   # only for state documents

[build-dependencies]
sortie-build = { git = "https://github.com/lynxr/sortie-sdk", tag = "v0.4.0" }

[lints.clippy]
await_holding_refcell_ref = "deny"   # catches a world borrow held across .await
```

- `build.rs`: `fn main() { sortie_build::scenario("my_mission", "scenario.lock.json").emit(); }`.
  The first argument is the scenario name; the path is relative to the crate's `Cargo.toml`.
- `src/lib.rs` starts with `sortie::include_scenario!(my_mission);`, which defines
  `pub mod my_mission` with the marker type `MyMission` and the symbol modules.
- `src/main.rs` is `sortie::main!(my_mission_logic::run);`: arguments, attach, reconnects.
- A private SDK repository needs credentials for cargo (`net.git-fetch-with-cli = true` in
  `.cargo/config.toml`, plus your git credential helper) and for uv: see the docs.

## The mission function

The examples in this skill use the `frontline` scenario of the sortie-scenario skill.

```rust
use sortie::prelude::*;

// lib.rs of the logic crate also has `sortie::include_scenario!(frontline);`
use frontline::{Frontline, groups, zones};

#[sortie::mission] // runs once per session of `frontline`
pub async fn run(ctx: Ctx<Frontline>, start: Start) -> sortie::Result<()> {
    let sam = ctx.group(groups::SAM_NORTH)?; // Group<Ground>, checked against the manifest
    sam.set_option(Alarm::Green).key("sam-dark").await?;

    if start.is_fresh() {
        ctx.message(Coalition::Blue)
            .text("SAM North is cold. Push when ready.")
            .secs(20)
            .key("intro")
            .await?;
    }

    // Evaluated on the local replica after every tick and every event: no RPC.
    ctx.wait_until(|w| {
        w.units()
            .coalition(Coalition::Blue)
            .air()
            .any_inside(zones::SAM_RING)
    })
    .await;
    sam.set_option(Alarm::Red).key("sam-hot").await?;

    // A state, not an event: still correct when the function runs again after a crash.
    ctx.wait_until(|w| w.group(&sam).alive_count() == 0).await;
    ctx.end_session(Outcome::BlueWin)
        .text("SAM North is down")
        .await
}
```

`#[sortie::mission]` checks the signature: `async fn`, `ctx: Ctx<M>` first, `start: Start`
second, return type `sortie::Result<()>`. Returning `Err` records a logic error with the call
site; the session goes on.

## Workflow

1. **Symbols first.** Everything the logic names (a group, zone, template, flag, airbase or
   menu) needs an `ident=` in `scenario.py`. Add it there, run `python scenario.py lock`, then
   build the logic. Groups added only by a `@sc.pydcs` hook have no symbol: reach them by DCS
   name in world queries (`w.group("Name")`, `.in_group("Name")`).
2. **Write the step replay-safe** (rules below), then `cargo build` and `cargo clippy`.
   Done when both pass and every `spawn_group` and `destroy` in the diff carries `.key(..)`.
3. **Run it in DCS** with `sortied --dev` and the logic's `--dev` (see the
   sortie-live-debugging skill). The public SDK has no tests without DCS: FakeDcs carries
   the engine and is not part of it yet, so `#[sortie::test]` is a compile error. Put pure
   decisions (which wave, which target) in plain functions and test them with ordinary
   `#[test]`.

## Rules

1. **Game logic lives in the Rust logic, never in the `.miz`.** The `.miz` that
   `scenario.py` builds holds the map side only (groups, units, statics, zones, weather,
   briefing, the warehouses' starting stock) and Sortie's bootstrap. What happens when,
   spawns, tasks, scoring, menus, marks and stock changes are all Rust. When the SDK lacks
   something, in this order:
   - a typed command or query (the API map below);
   - a catalog call: its generated wrapper (`ctx.dcs().land().height(p)`); with the cargo
     feature `dcs-raw` also by path (`ctx.dcs().call("land.getHeight")..`) and a batch of
     many calls in one frame (`ctx.dcs().batch()`);
   - a raw DCS task table, `group.set_task(Task::raw(table))`: any group takes it, for what
     the typed tasks lack (a stop, tasks at waypoints, a ship's route: references/api.md);
   - tell the Sortie team what is missing.
   A DO SCRIPT added through a `@sc.pydcs` hook is only for a third-party script the
   mission must keep (Sortie does not check it), never for the mission's own logic. The
   build warns about every such script (also an init script or a LUA PREDICATE), and the
   template's `scenario.py` sets `do_scripts="deny"`, which fails the build.
2. **Key every command whose repetition matters.** `spawn_group` and `destroy` always: they
   are refused without a key when `sortied` runs with `--dev` and when the logic runs with
   `--dev`. Key messages, smoke, flags and menu commands that a replay must not repeat. Key
   semantics:
   - the scope is the session: within it, a key that already ran returns the stored result
     without reaching DCS (a replayed spawn returns the same `Group`);
   - a key names a step, so it is the same on every run: a literal (`"red-cap-1"`) or built
     from a deterministic counter (`format!("wave-{n}")`), never from model time, a random
     number or an Eid;
   - one key, one command: reusing a key for a different body (other text, other target) fails
     with `sortie::invalid` ("key `k` was already used for a different command in session ...");
   - a keyed command that timed out after reaching DCS is not sent again on retry with the
     same key: the retry waits for the late result;
   - a mission restart is a new session: keys start empty again.
3. **Wait on states, not events,** when the condition is visible in the world:
   `ctx.wait_until(|w| w.group(&sam).alive_count() == 0)`. A replay sees the state; it never
   sees an event that happened before it subscribed.
4. **Delays that must survive a logic restart are named timers:**
   `ctx.timer("cap-delay", mins(10))`. `ctx.sleep` starts over after a restart.
5. **Campaign changes go inside `ctx.once_per_turn`.** After a mission restart the turn is
   played again in a new session; `once_per_turn` keeps a kill from being counted twice in one
   turn. `ctx.once` is per session.
6. **Short borrows.** Take `ctx.world()` and `StateDoc::get()` in a statement or a block that
   ends before the next `.await`. A borrow held across `.await` stops the replica from updating
   (the runtime records "the world replica is borrowed across an `.await`").
7. **Never block the thread.** No `std::thread::sleep`, blocking I/O or long CPU loops: ticks
   stop, and after 4096 unread messages the engine detaches the logic (it exits with code 0).
   Wait with `ctx.sleep`, `ctx.timer`, `ctx.wait_until`.
8. **Background work is `ctx.spawn`.** Its tasks end with the session; an `Err` or a panic in
   one is recorded with its call site and the other tasks keep running. No `std::thread`, no
   runtime of your own.

## Start kinds

```rust
match start {
    // First session of this build: the world is as the manifest describes it.
    Start::Fresh => {}
    // The mission was reloaded (same turn): a fresh world, fresh keys and `once`s;
    // `once_per_turn` and the campaign state remember the earlier session.
    Start::Restart => {
        ctx.message(Coalition::Blue)
            .text("Mission restarted")
            .key("restarted")
            .await?;
    }
    // The logic process restarted inside a running session (crash, or you restarted it
    // after a rebuild): the world is as it is now; keys, `once` and timers remember.
    // `Resumed` (the engine resumed the session after its own restart) is not sent yet;
    // treat it the same way.
    Start::AfterCrash | Start::Resumed => {}
}
```

| `Start` | When | The world | Keys, `once`, timers | `once_per_turn`, campaign state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Fresh` | first session of this build (turn) | as in the manifest | empty | as stored |
| `Restart` | the mission was reloaded (`scenario.py restart`, or the same build loaded again) | as in the manifest | empty (new session) | remembered |
| `AfterCrash` | the logic process restarted in the running session (crash, or restarted after a rebuild) | as it is now | remembered | remembered |
| `Resumed` | the engine resumed a session after its own restart (not sent yet) | as it is now | remembered | remembered |

A replay-safe mission needs no branch on `Start` except for player-facing extras (a briefing on
`Fresh`, a notice on `Restart`).

## API map

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| a scenario group | `ctx.group(groups::X)?` → `Group<Ground/Air/Helo/Ship>`; `set_option(Alarm::Red / Roe::..)`, `destroy()`, `push_task`/`set_task` (`Task::cap/orbit/rtb` for air and helicopters; `Task::ground_route(..)` for ground groups, API revision 3; a raw DCS task table, `Task::raw(..)`, for any group) |
| spawn | `ctx.spawn_group(templates::X)` or `templates::X.named("..")`, then `.from_airbase(airbases::Y, StartType::..)`, `.at(Vec3, heading_rad)` (every unit faces `heading_rad`, the formation is not turned) or `.at_formation(Vec3, heading_rad)` (API revision 3: the formation turns as one body, each unit keeps its heading offset), `.key(..)` → `Group<K>` |
| tell players | `ctx.message(Coalition::Blue / &group / press.group / sortie::MessageTarget::All).text(..).secs(..)` |
| read the world | `ctx.world()`, `w.units().coalition(..).air().in_zone(zones::X).count()`, `w.players()`, `w.group(&g).alive_count()` |
| wait | `ctx.wait_until(pred)`, `ctx.timer(name, dur)`, `ctx.sleep(dur)`, `ctx.until_session_end()` |
| react | `ctx.events().of::<v1::Dead>().in_group(&g)`; `use sortie::proto::v1;` |
| F10 menu | `ctx.menu(Coalition::Blue).per_group().command(menus::X).key(..).await?`, then `.presses()` |
| F10 menu tree (one group, sub-menus) | `ctx.menus().tree("jtac").to(Audience::group(..)).command(id, label).submenu(label, \|s\| ..).await?`, then `.presses()`; needs `#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 1, event_rev = 1)]`; a level of more than 10 entries pages itself (`More...`; on the tree's root level `More... (<tree name>)`) unless `.overflow(Overflow::Reject)` |
| flags | `ctx.flag(flags::X).set(true)`, `.get()` → `i32` |
| remember | `ctx.state::<T>("name")` (campaign), `ctx.state_in::<T>(v1::StateScope::Turn, ..)`, `ctx.once`, `ctx.once_per_turn` |
| results | `ctx.report().set("key", value)`, `ctx.end_session(Outcome::BlueWin).text(..)` |
| data for a web site (live map, campaign page) | `ctx.publish("front", &value).await?` (any `Serialize`; the engine serves it at `GET /api/v1/docs/<logic>/front`), `ctx.unpublish(name)`; needs `#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 3)]` |
| a web site asks the logic to do something | `let mut reqs = ctx.api().action("send_cap")?;` then `while let Some(req) = reqs.next().await { .. req.reply(&value)? / req.fail(422, why)? }` (called as `POST /api/v1/actions/<logic>/send_cap` with an `operator` token; answer within 10 s; a dropped request is 500); needs `#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 3)]` |
| airbase owner, auto capture, radio silence | `ctx.airbase_control([airbases::X, airbases::Y]).owner(Coalition::Red).auto_capture(false).radio_silent(true).key(..)` (1..=32 bases, one frame) → per-base `before` / `after` / `error()`; the world has the owner at once; needs `#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 3)]` |
| airbase owner changed (any cause) | `ctx.events().of::<v1::AirbaseOwnerChanged>()`, `.airbase(..)`, `.cause(v1::OwnerChangeCause::Captured)`; one per change (DCS capture, `airbase_control`, a read of DCS); an owner another script changed without an event comes only from a read: poll `ctx.airbases_state(..)`; needs `#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 3, event_rev = 2)]` |
| airbase parking, runways, control state | `ctx.airbase(airbases::X).parking().available_only()` → `Vec<ParkingSpot>`, `.runways()` → `Vec<Runway>`, `.state()` → `AirbaseState`; many: `ctx.airbases_parking([..])` / `airbases_runways` / `airbases_state` → per-base `value` / `error()`; reads, no key, API revision 3 |
| warehouse stock | `ctx.warehouse(airbases::X).stock()` → `WarehouseStock { aircraft, weapons, liquids }` (`StockClass::Unlimited` or `Limited(name -> n)`); `.items([..])` / `.liquids()` count only those; many: `ctx.warehouses_stock([..])` → per-warehouse `value` / `error()`; a read, no key, API revision 3 |
| change warehouse stock, move it between warehouses | `ctx.warehouse_op().transfer(airbases::X, airbases::Y, "weapons.missiles.AIM_120C", 6.0).add(airbases::Y, Liquid::JetFuel, 5000.0).key(..)` (also `.set`, `.remove`; 1..=16 changes, one frame, all or nothing) → `StockChanges { applied, changes }` (per change `outcome`: `Done`, `NotEnough`, `Unlimited`, `Aliased`, ...); every warehouse_op needs a key in dev, sets too; name an item in one form per command; API revision 3 |
| the names DCS gives warehouse items, name <-> wsType (check a campaign's items before stocking; no `Warehouse.getResourceMap` catalog entry) | `ctx.item_names()` → `ItemNames` (`.ws_type_of("weapons.missiles.AIM_120C")`, `.names_of([4, 4, 7, 106])`, `.knows(..)`); `.items([..])` looks up only those (`unknown` for the rest); read from the running DCS once per DCS process (`cached` after); a read that takes no key (`.key(..)` is `Error::Invalid`), API revision 3 |
| a DCS function with no typed operation | `ctx.dcs().land().surface_type(p)`, `ctx.dcs().airbase(airbases::X).callsign()`, `ctx.dcs().sounds().out_sound(..)`; needs `#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 1)]` |
| a ground group drives somewhere (a convoy, a route along roads) | `convoy.set_task(Task::ground_route([RoutePoint::on_road(p), ..]))` (API revision 3); a stop or what the route lacks: `Task::raw(..)`; references/api.md, "A ground group's route" |
| the road between two map points (a convoy's distance, a stop on the way) | `ctx.dcs().land().path_on_roads("roads", from.north, from.east, to.north, to.east)` → `Option<Vec<MapPoint>>`, start to end; class heavy (one at a time, 2 per second, its own DCS-time budget, ends at most 300 km apart, never in a batch); needs `#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 3)]`: references/api.md, "A road path" |
| the length and ends of a road path without its points; a few of its turning points for a route | `ctx.dcs().land().road_path("roads", from, to, Some(8.0), None)` → `Option<RoadPath>` (`count`, `length_m`, `first`/`last`, `start_gap_m`/`end_gap_m`, `points` capped with both ends, `thinned`), summarised by the Lua layer inside DCS; class heavy; needs `#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 3)]`: references/api.md, "The summary of a road path" |

Signatures, defaults and an example for each: [references/api.md](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-mission-logic/references/api.md).

## More

- [references/patterns.md](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-mission-logic/references/patterns.md): a long multiplayer mission (thousands of
  units, players joining and leaving, AI waves, polling, scores) and the anti-patterns.
- [references/errors.md](https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/agents/sortie-mission-logic/references/errors.md): every `sortie::*` error code, the build and
  attach errors, and their fixes.
- Docs (Russian): https://lynxr.github.io/sortie-sdk/. Scenario side: the sortie-scenario skill. Running in DCS:
  the sortie-live-debugging skill.

<!-- source: agents/sortie-mission-logic/references/api.md -->

# Sortie SDK API reference (for agents)

Everything below is in `sortie::prelude::*` unless a path is given. Event and state enums live
in `sortie::proto::v1` (`use sortie::proto::v1;`). The examples use the `frontline` scenario
(module `frontline`, marker `Frontline`).

## Commands

Every write returns a `Cmd<..>`. Nothing happens until it is awaited; `.await` gives
`sortie::Result<Output>`.

```rust
ctx.smoke(zones::OBJECTIVE.center(), SmokeColor::Red)
    .key("smoke-obj")
    .await?;
ctx.flag(flags::SAM_DOWN)
    .set(true)
    .key("flag-sam-down")
    .await?;

let cap = ctx
    .spawn_group(templates::RED_CAP.named("Red CAP 1"))
    .from_airbase(airbases::MAYKOP, StartType::Runway)
    .key("red-cap-1") // spawn and destroy: always keyed
    .await?; // Group<Air>
cap.push_task(
    Task::cap(zones::SAM_RING)
        .altitude(ft(25_000))
        .speed(kts(420)),
)
.timeout(secs(5))
.await?;
cap.set_option(Roe::WeaponFree).await?;

let armor = ctx.group(groups::RED_ARMOR)?;
armor.destroy().key("armor-despawn").await?;
```

Options on every command:

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `.key(impl Into<String>)` | idempotency key, scope: the session (see the rules in SKILL.md) |
| `.timeout(Duration)` | fail with `sortie::timeout` if DCS has not answered; default 10 s, 30 s for `spawn_group` and `destroy` |
| `.on_pause(v1::PausePolicy::Fail)` | fail with `sortie::paused` instead of waiting while the simulation is paused (default: wait) |
| `.after(&other_cmd)` | run only after `other_cmd` (not yet awaited) completed |
| `.lane(v1::Lane::..)` | scheduling lane; the default fits the command |
| `.id()` | the command id, shown in errors |

| Command | Output | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ctx.message(to).text(..).secs(u32).clear_view()` | `()` | `to`: `Coalition`, `&Group<K>`, `AnyGroup` (a menu press), `sortie::MessageTarget::All`; 10 s by default |
| `ctx.smoke(at, SmokeColor::Red)` | `()` | `at`: a `MapPoint` (on the ground) or a `Vec3` |
| `ctx.flag(flags::X).set(v)` / `.get()` | `()` / `i32` | `v`: `bool` or `i32` |
| `ctx.spawn_group(t)` | `Group<K>` | `t`: `templates::X` or `templates::X.named("Name")`; then `.from_airbase(airbases::Y, StartType::{Runway, Hot, Cold, Air})`, `.at(Vec3, heading_rad)` (unit 1 at the point, the other units moved with their template offsets, not turned, and **every unit facing `heading_rad`**) or `.at_formation(Vec3, heading_rad)` (API revision 3: the formation turned as one body about unit 1 by `heading_rad` minus the template's reference heading, `Template.heading_rad` else unit 1's, each unit facing its template heading plus that turn, so the differences between the units stay); both give the group one route point at the point (the template's route is not carried over); without either, the template's own placement. Switching a keyed `.at` to `.at_formation` is another command: give it a new key (the same key is `Error::Invalid`). Default name `<template name>#<session4>-<n>`, units `<group>-<k>`; `.named` fails with `sortie::name_conflict` if a live group has the name. The engine paces spawns (currently 2 groups or 24 units a second), so a big wave takes time. |
| `group.set_option(o)` | `()` | `o`: `Alarm::{Auto, Green, Red}` or `Roe::{WeaponFree, OpenFireWeaponFree, OpenFire, ReturnFire, WeaponHold}` |
| `group.destroy()` | `()` | despawn; no DEAD event follows (a `UnitGone` does) |
| `group.push_task(task)` / `group.set_task(task)` | `()` | every group; push on the task stack or replace it. `Task::cap` / `Task::orbit` / `Task::rtb` are for `Group<Air>` and `Group<Helo>`, `Task::ground_route` for `Group<Ground>` (a task of the wrong kind does not compile, except RTB, which the engine refuses: `sortie::invalid`); `Task::raw` for any group, and the only task of a naval group |
| `ctx.menu(c).command(menus::X)` | `MenuCommand<S>` | see Menus |
| `ctx.end_session(outcome).text(..)` | `()` | ends the session (the turn); succeeds even if the session ends first |

Tasks (`Task` is in the prelude):

| Task | Defaults |
| --- | --- |
| `Task::cap(zones::X).altitude(Length).speed(Speed)` | 6000 m, 420 kt |
| `Task::orbit(MapPoint).altitude(..).speed(..).race_track(MapPoint)` | 6000 m, 350 kt, a circle without `race_track` |
| `Task::rtb(airbases::X)` | |
| `Task::ground_route([RoutePoint::on_road(p), RoutePoint::new(p, GroundFormation::Vee).speed(..)]).speed(Speed)` | API revision 3, `Group<Ground>` only; 20 km/h; 1 to 256 points |
| `Task::raw(sortie::proto::LuaValue)` | a DCS task table, for any group; the engine refuses Lua code in it (`Script`, `ScriptFile`, a `condition` string, a `file` string: `sortie::rejected`, capability `dev_eval`) and NaN or infinities (`sortie::invalid`) |

### A ground group's route

A ground group drives a typed route, `Task::ground_route` (API revision 3: the mission declares
`#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 3)]`; `RoutePoint` and `GroundFormation` are in the prelude):

```rust
let armor = ctx.group(groups::RED_ARMOR)?; // Group<Ground>
let objective = zones::OBJECTIVE.center();
let route = Task::ground_route([
    // along the roads to a point 3 km south of the objective
    RoutePoint::on_road(objective.offset(-3_000.0, 0.0)),
    // the last leg straight across the fields, in a vee, at 15 km/h
    RoutePoint::new(objective, GroundFormation::Vee).speed(kmh(15)),
])
.speed(kmh(40)); // for the points that set no speed (default 20 km/h)
armor.set_task(route).key("armor-to-objective").await?;
```

- The engine builds DCS's `Mission` task in the shape the Mission Editor writes for vehicles,
  with a first point where the group's first live unit stands in the frame DCS takes the task
  (the formation and speed of the first route point). Do not add a start point yourself.
- A point's formation and speed are those of the leg that ends at it (the editor's model: a
  leg keeps to the roads when both its ends are "On Road", and is timed by the speed of the
  point it ends at).
- Formations: `RoutePoint::on_road` (along the roads), `off_road` (straight, in column),
  `on_railroads` (trains), `RoutePoint::new(p, GroundFormation::{Rank, Cone, Vee, Diamond,
  EchelonLeft, EchelonRight})` (straight, in that formation).
- Speed: the point's, else the route's, else 20 km/h.
- Points are `MapPoint`s: `zones::X.center()`, a unit's `pos.map_point()`, a point of
  `ctx.dcs().land().path_on_roads(..)` ("DCS calls", "A road path") or of its summary
  `ctx.dcs().land().road_path(..)` ("The summary of a road path"). 1 to 256 points; a longer
  route is `sortie::invalid`. Between two "On Road" points the Mission Editor lays the road
  path itself (that DCS drives it so is `AI-L4`), so a route needs only the places where it
  turns or stops: of a road path, its end (`path.last()`) or a few points where it turns. Never
  map every point of a road path into the route: a long path can have more points than the
  limit, and each would be a leg of its own. The whole path is for measuring the way.
- `Group<Ground>` only: for an aircraft, a helicopter or a ship it does not compile (through
  `Task::from(route)` the engine refuses it, `sortie::invalid`). A logic below revision 3 gets
  `sortie::revision`, an older engine `sortie::engine_too_old`; nothing is sent.
- How DCS drives it (which road, reaching the nearest road, a point in water or off the map) is
  not measured live yet: live check `AI-L4` of the wide probe.

What the typed route lacks (a stop, tasks at waypoints, a `Custom` formation, a ship's route)
goes in a raw DCS task table, `Task::raw(..)`, which any group takes:

```rust
use sortie::proto::LuaTable;
use sortie::proto::LuaValue;

// DCS's "Hold" task stops the group where it stands; the SDK has no typed stop.
let stop = LuaTable::new()
    .with("id", "Hold")
    .with("params", LuaTable::new());
let armor = ctx.group(groups::RED_ARMOR)?;
armor.push_task(Task::raw(LuaValue::table(stop))).await?;
```

- A waypoint of a raw `Mission` task is `{type = "Turning Point", action = "On Road" | "Off
  Road", x, y, speed}`: `x` north and `y` east in map metres (`MapPoint.north` / `.east`;
  `Vec3.x` / `.z`), `speed` in m/s; start it where the group stands, as the editor does. How
  DCS drives a raw route is live check `AI-L3`.
- The engine checks a raw table for safety only; a malformed task can fail in DCS
  (`sortie::lua_error`) or be ignored by DCS without an error.
- SDK 0.3.0 and older had `push_task` / `set_task` on aircraft groups only, and no typed route.

Units and geometry: `m`, `km`, `ft`, `nm` → `Length`; `kts`, `mps`, `kmh` → `Speed`; `secs`,
`mins`, `hours` → `Duration`. `MapPoint { north, east }` (metres, map axes): `.alt(Length)` →
`Vec3`, `.distance(p)`, `.offset(north_m, east_m)`, `.bearing_to(p)`,
`.toward(bearing_rad, Length)`. `Vec3 { x: north, y: up, z: east }`: `.map_point()`. Zones:
`zones::X.center()`, `zones::X.contains(p)`.

Groups: `ctx.group(groups::X)?` returns the live group or `sortie::not_in_world` (no live unit:
late activation, destroyed) or `sortie::unknown_symbol` (the running mission lacks the symbol).
`Group<K>` is bound to one life of the group: a group respawned under the same name is a new
handle. Methods: `eid()`, `name()`, `alive_count()`, `is_alive()`, `any()` → `AnyGroup`.

## Keys in loops

```rust
for n in 1..=3 {
    ctx.timer(&format!("wave-{n}-delay"), mins(5)).await; // deadline stored in the engine
    let wave = ctx
        .spawn_group(templates::RED_CAP)
        .from_airbase(airbases::MAYKOP, StartType::Hot)
        .key(format!("wave-{n}")) // same n, same key: never spawned twice
        .await?;
    ctx.wait_until(|w| w.group(&wave).alive_count() == 0).await;
}
```

After a logic restart the loop runs again from `n = 1`: passed timers return at once, keyed
spawns return their stored groups, and the waits on dead groups pass. The script fast-forwards
to where it was.

## Once

`Campaign` here and below is a state document type:
`#[derive(Default, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct Campaign { pub sams_killed: u32 }`.

```rust
let campaign = ctx.state::<Campaign>("campaign").await?; // campaign scope: kept across turns

// Once per session: skipped when the function runs again after a crash.
ctx.once("briefing", async |ctx| {
    ctx.message(Coalition::Blue)
        .text("Destroy SAM North.")
        .secs(30)
        .await
})
.await?;

// Once per turn (= per mission build): also skipped after a mission restart.
ctx.wait_until(|w| w.group(&groups::SAM_NORTH).alive_count() == 0)
    .await;
ctx.once_per_turn("count-sam-kill", async |ctx| {
    campaign.update(|c| c.sams_killed += 1).await?;
    ctx.flag(flags::SAM_DOWN).set(true).await
})
.await?;
```

`ctx.once(name, f)` and `ctx.once_per_turn(name, f)` return `Ok(Some(value))` when `f` ran and
`Ok(None)` when it had run before. The mark is written after `f` succeeded: an `Err` from `f`
leaves it unmarked.

## Waiting

```rust
ctx.sleep(secs(30)).await; // model time; stops while paused; starts over after a crash
ctx.timer("cap-delay", mins(10)).await; // named: the deadline survives a logic restart

let blue_in_front = |w: &World| {
    w.units()
        .coalition(Coalition::Blue)
        .in_zone(zones::FRONT)
        .any()
};
ctx.wait_until(blue_in_front).await;

let red_left = ctx.world().group(&groups::RED_ARMOR).alive_count(); // a short borrow
ctx.report().set("red_armor_left", red_left);

// Any end: the logic, the time limit, a restart. Code after it runs only up to the next
// .await; then the session's tasks are aborted.
let end = ctx.until_session_end().await;
eprintln!("session ended: {:?} ({:?})", end.outcome, end.reason); // the logic's stderr
```

- `wait_until` checks its predicate now, after every tick (10 per second) and after every
  event. Keep the predicate cheap; see patterns.md for thousands of units.
- `sleep`, `timer`: model time; a pause stops them.
- `until_session_end()` → `SessionEnd { outcome: Option<Outcome>, text, reason }`, with
  `sortie::EndReason`: `Logic`, `TimeLimit`, `Restart`, `MissionUnloaded`, `EngineShutdown`,
  `Replaced`, `Disconnected`, `Unspecified`. When the session ends, pending commands fail with
  `sortie::session_ended` (not a logic error) and every task of the session is aborted.
- `ctx.model_time()`, `ctx.paused()`, `ctx.is_session_ended()`, `ctx.session_id()`,
  `ctx.turn()` (the build id of the running mission). Model time is seconds since the mission
  started (`timer.getTime`), standing still while paused, never the time of day (a mission that
  starts at 09:00 reads about 60 a minute in, not 32 460); ticks, `sleep`, `timer` and every
  event's `model_time` use it. The time of day: `ctx.dcs().timer().abs_time()`.

World queries (`ctx.world()` or the `wait_until` argument, a `&World`):

| Query | Methods |
| --- | --- |
| `w.units()` (live units) | filters `.coalition(c)`, `.air()`, `.planes()`, `.helos()`, `.ground()`, `.ships()`, `.statics()`, `.any_category()`, `.dead()`, `.including_dead()`, `.players()`, `.in_group(&g)`, `.of_type("F-16C_50")`, `.in_zone(zones::X)`, `.within(point, km(5))`; results `.count()`, `.any()`, `.first()`, `.iter()`, `.eids()`, `.nearest_to(point)`, `.inside(&zone)`, `.any_inside(zone)`, `.count_inside(zone)` |
| `w.players()`, `w.statics()` | the same query, preset |
| `w.group(&g)` | `g`: a `Group<K>`, `&groups::X`, a DCS group name; `.exists()`, `.alive_count()`, `.size()`, `.is_dead()`, `.center()`, `.any_inside(z)`, `.count_inside(z)`, `.all_inside(z)`, `.units()`, `.alive_units()`; a missing group counts as empty |
| `w.airbase_by_ident("MAYKOP")`, `w.airbase_by_name(..)`, `w.airbases()` | airbases with their current owner |

An entity (`&sortie::world::Entity`) has `name`, `type_name`, `coalition`, `category`,
`group_name`, `pos: Option<Vec3>`, `velocity`, `heading`, `player: Option<String>`, `life`,
`dead`.

## Events

```rust
let sam = ctx.group(groups::SAM_NORTH)?;
// Subscribe first, then act: a stream only sees events from the moment it was made.
let mut deaths = ctx.events().of::<v1::Dead>().in_group(&sam);
ctx.spawn(async move |ctx| {
    while let Some(dead) = deaths.next().await {
        let name = dead.initiator.map(|u| u.name).unwrap_or_default();
        ctx.message(Coalition::Blue)
            .text(format!("{name} destroyed"))
            .secs(10)
            .await?;
    }
    Ok(()) // `None`: the session ended
});
```

- `ctx.events()` → `Events`, `.next().await` → `Option<v1::Event>` (`ev.kind`,
  `ev.model_time`, `ev.seq`); `None` once the session ended.
- `.of::<E>()` keeps one type; filters `.in_group(&g)` (a `Group<K>` matches only its own life;
  a `GroupRef` or a name matches whatever group has it now), `.coalition(c)`, `.filter(|e| ..)`.
  They test the event's subject: the initiator, `unit` for `PlayerEnteredUnit`, `last_known`
  for `UnitGone`.
- Types: `Birth`, `Dead`, `UnitLost`, `Kill`, `Hit` (the initiator may be missing), `Shot`,
  `Takeoff`, `Land`, `BaseCaptured`, `Mark`, `PlayerEnteredUnit` (built from BIRTH and the
  player name: multiplayer clients do not get a reliable DCS event), `UnitGone` (left the world
  without DEAD: despawned, missing from a sample), `MenuPressed`, `PlayerConnected`,
  `PlayerDisconnected`, `PlayerChangedSlot`, `ChatMessage`, `SimulationPaused`,
  `SimulationResumed`, `Gap` (events were lost; the replica was resynced), `Unknown`; of event
  revision 1 `ResourceEnded`, `CapabilityChanged`; of event revision 2 `AirbaseOwnerChanged`
  ("Airbases" below). A kind above the logic's event revision never arrives
  (`#[sortie::mission(event_rev = N)]`, capped by the engine's: `ctx.event_rev()`); `.of::<E>()`
  logs a warning then.
- A `Mark` (F10 map mark) carries model time like every event since 0.4.0; DCS's own `time`
  of it (the time of day, per the Hoggit wiki; live check EVT-L18) is `Mark.dcs_time` (API
  revision 3). With a Lua layer older than 0.4.0 (no `sortie install`) `model_time` of a mark
  is still the time of day and `dcs_time` is empty; the engine's clock is not affected.
- Each event is applied to the replica before your code sees it: in a `Dead` handler the unit
  already counts as dead.
- A stream sees events from the moment it was created. A stream that falls more than 1024
  events behind skips the oldest and logs a warning. Holes in `ev.seq` are not losses (a
  filtered stream sees part of the journal); only `Gap` reports a loss.
- Which DCS event it was (engine API revision 1): `ev.dcs_event()` (`v1::DcsEvent`, the
  `world.event` entry by name; `Unspecified` for engine and hook events, and for an entry the
  enum lacks, which `ev.dcs_name` then names). `Dead` comes from DEAD, CRASH and PILOT_DEAD,
  `Takeoff` from TAKEOFF and RUNWAY_TAKEOFF, `Land` from LAND and RUNWAY_TOUCH: pick with
  `.from_dcs(v1::DcsEvent::Crash)` (repeatable: any of) and read the entry with
  `.next_with_dcs_event()` → `Option<(E, v1::DcsEvent)>`. Against a 0.1.0 engine
  `.from_dcs` matches nothing. From API revision 1 (`#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 1)]`) a
  pilot's death no longer kills the unit in the world; at revision 0 (the macro's default) the
  `Dead` of PILOT_DEAD reads `dead = true` as in 0.1.0 and the logic's world holds the unit
  dead for good. A player leaving a unit clears `EntitySnap.player` (every revision).
- Weapons and ejected crew are no world entities but have Eids (engine API revision 1, every
  revision of the logic): `Shot`, `Hit` and `Kill` of one weapon carry the same `weapon.eid`
  (0: no weapon object, only `weapon_type`, or a unit in a collision); pilots and seats in the
  `ctx` of `S_EVENT_EJECTION` / `S_EVENT_LANDING_AFTER_EJECTION` are snaps with Eids (seat and
  pilot differ). `Obj::weapon(&w)` / `Obj::snap(&s)` (`Option<Obj>`, `None` for Eid 0) select
  one for `ctx.destroy(..)` while DCS still has it (`caps::DESTROY_WEAPON`); afterwards, or 30 s
  after a weapon's first hit, `Error::Gone`. No `UnitGone` follows.
- Every other DCS event is `v1::Unknown` with `ctx: Option<v1::EventContext>`: `initiator`,
  `target` (snaps with Eids; Eid 0 for an object the engine cannot name), `weapon`, `place`
  (`airbase`, also for a ship's deck, or `entity`), `weapon_type`, `text` (or the comment),
  `pos`, `coalition`,
  `group_eid`, `idx`, `extra` (every other key as data, two levels), `extra_objects` (objects
  under other keys), `foreign` (another script raised it through `world.onEvent`: data only).
  `.in_group` / `.coalition` test `ctx.initiator`. `fields` is the raw table in the 0.1.0
  shape, the 0.1.0 keys only: read new keys from `ctx`.

```rust
// Wrecks only: DCS also sends the pilot's death as a Dead while the aircraft still flies.
let mut wrecks = ctx
    .events()
    .of::<v1::Dead>()
    .from_dcs(v1::DcsEvent::Dead)
    .from_dcs(v1::DcsEvent::Crash);
let mut starts = ctx
    .events()
    .of::<v1::Unknown>()
    .from_dcs(v1::DcsEvent::EngineStartup);
if let Some((dead, entry)) = wrecks.next_with_dcs_event().await {
    let name = dead.initiator.map(|u| u.name).unwrap_or_default();
    eprintln!("{name}: {entry:?}");
}
if let Some(start) = starts.next().await {
    let who = start.ctx.and_then(|c| c.initiator).map(|u| u.name);
    eprintln!("engines started: {who:?}");
}
```

- FakeDcs: `dcs.raise_event(FakeEvent::dcs("S_EVENT_ENGINE_STARTUP").initiator("Viper-1")
  .key("comment", ".."))`; another script's event: `FakeEvent::foreign(id)`.

## Menus

```rust
let smoke = ctx
    .menu(Coalition::Blue)
    .per_group() // every blue player group gets the command; a press carries the group
    .command(menus::SMOKE_OBJECTIVE)
    .key("menu-smoke")
    .await?;
ctx.spawn(async move |ctx| {
    let mut presses = smoke.presses();
    while let Some(p) = presses.next().await {
        ctx.smoke(zones::OBJECTIVE.center(), SmokeColor::Red)
            .await?;
        ctx.message(p.group)
            .text("Red smoke on the objective")
            .secs(10)
            .await?;
    }
    Ok(())
});

let sitrep = ctx
    .menu(Coalition::Blue)
    .command(menus::SITREP)
    .key("menu-sitrep")
    .await?;
ctx.spawn(async move |ctx| {
    let mut presses = sitrep.presses();
    while presses.next().await.is_some() {
        let left = ctx.world().group(&groups::SAM_NORTH).alive_count();
        ctx.message(Coalition::Blue)
            .text(format!("SAM North: {left} alive"))
            .await?;
    }
    Ok(())
});
```

- `ctx.menu(coalition)` is one command for the whole coalition; a press is a
  `CoalitionPress { coalition, model_time }`. `.per_group()` installs it for every player group
  of the coalition (those present now and each new one at its first player BIRTH); a press is
  a `GroupPress { group: AnyGroup, coalition, model_time }`, and `ctx.message(p.group)` answers
  that group.
- Label and sub-menu path come from `scenario.py` (`sc.menu(ident, label, path=[..])`).
- Presses are queued from the moment the command is installed. Each press goes to one
  `Presses` stream. `menu.remove()` removes the command. Adding the same command twice changes
  nothing in DCS.

## Menu trees

`ctx.menus()` builds F10 radio menu trees by name (API revision 1): commands and sub-menus for
everyone (the default), a coalition or one group. A tree is a resource of the session like a
drawing; a put with an existing name brings that tree to the new spec.

```rust
#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 1, event_rev = 1)] // trees: API rev 1; their presses: event rev 1
pub async fn run(ctx: Ctx<Frontline>, _start: Start) -> sortie::Result<()> {
    // One group's tree: SUSPENDED until a player takes a slot of "Viper 1"; the engine installs
    // it for the group's id, removes it when the slot empties and follows a dynamic slot.
    let jtac = ctx
        .menus()
        .tree("jtac/viper-1")
        .to(Audience::group(GroupSel::name("Viper 1")))
        .under(["JTAC"])
        .command("check-in", "Check in")
        .submenu("Smoke", |s| {
            s.command_arg("smoke-red", "Red", "red")
                .command_arg("smoke-green", "Green", "green")
        })
        .await?;
    let mut presses = jtac.presses();
    while let Some(p) = presses.next().await {
        if p.item.starts_with("smoke-") {
            let color = if p.arg == "red" {
                SmokeColor::Red
            } else {
                SmokeColor::Green
            };
            ctx.smoke(zones::OBJECTIVE.center(), color).await?;
        }
        if let Some(group) = p.group {
            ctx.message(group).text("Copy").await?;
        }
    }
    ctx.menus().remove("jtac/viper-1").await?;
    ctx.end_session(Outcome::Draw).await
}
```

- `tree(name)` then `.to(..)`, `.under([..])`, `.command(id, label)`, `.command_arg(id, label,
  arg)`, `.manifest_command(id, menus::X)`, `.submenu(label, |s| ..)`, `.overflow(..)`,
  `.ttl(..)`; the result is `MenuTree { change, dcs_calls, resource, warnings }` with
  `.presses()` and `.is_suspended()`. A press is `TreePress { tree, item, arg, ident, group,
  coalition, model_time }`; `ctx.menus().presses(name)` reads presses of any tree.
- DCS shows 10 entries per level. A longer level of the tree is paged by default
  (`sortie::menu_tree::Overflow::Page`): 9 entries and a sub-menu `More...` with the rest,
  paged the same way. The page of the tree's root level reads `More... (<tree name>)`: that
  level is shared with other trees and DCS finds an entry by its label path, so each tree's
  page there needs its own label; pick tree names a player can read. Do not split a long list
  into sub-menus by hand for that, and do not look for the page in presses: a press of an
  entry on a page carries that entry's own `item` and `arg`. Pages cost DCS calls, not nodes.
  `.overflow(Overflow::Reject)` refuses such a level instead.
- `Error::Invalid`: two entries with one label on one level, an entry labelled like a page
  of its level (`More...`, on the root level also `More... (<tree name>)`) on a level that
  pages, more than 10 entries on a level with `Overflow::Reject`, more than 200 nodes, a
  command without an id.
- `change`: `Unchanged` (equal, no DCS call), `Updated` (only the changed entries and the ones
  after them on their level are sent again), `Replaced` (another audience or `under`).
- A group tree follows the slot: SUSPENDED while nobody occupies the group, installed by the
  engine when a player takes a slot, removed when it empties, installed again for a dynamic
  slot's new group id. A group given by Eid ends with `ResourceEnded{SOURCE_GONE}` with the
  group.
- `remove(name)`, `remove_prefix(p)`, `clear()`; menus go when the session ends. The 0.1.0
  `ctx.menu(..)` commands are registered too (`sortie:menu/..` in `ctx.world().resources()`).

## Flags

```rust
let sam_down = ctx.flag(flags::SAM_DOWN);
sam_down.set(1).key("sam-down").await?; // bool or i32
let value: i32 = sam_down.get().await?; // reads DCS (a mission trigger may change it too)
```

## State and results

```rust
#[derive(Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Progress {
    waves_sent: u32,
}
// Campaign scope (default): kept across turns; the generator can read it.
let campaign = ctx.state::<Campaign>("campaign").await?;
// Turn scope: survives mission restarts of this build; session scope: this session only.
let turn = ctx
    .state_in::<Progress>(v1::StateScope::Turn, "progress")
    .await?;

turn.update(|p| p.waves_sent += 1).await?; // compare-and-swap, retried on conflict
let killed = campaign.get().sams_killed; // a local copy; do not hold `get()` across .await
ctx.report().set("sams_killed", killed); // MissionResults.report_json, read by `results`
```

| Scope | Lives | API |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `v1::StateScope::Session` | this session | `ctx.state_in::<T>(v1::StateScope::Session, name)` |
| `v1::StateScope::Turn` | this build (turn), across mission restarts | `ctx.state_in::<T>(v1::StateScope::Turn, name)` |
| `v1::StateScope::Campaign` | across turns of the scenario | `ctx.state::<T>(name)` |

`T: Serialize + DeserializeOwned + Default` (`#[derive(Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]`; the
crate needs `serde` with the `derive` feature). `StateDoc<T>`: `get()` (local copy),
`update(|t| ..)` (compare-and-swap; on a conflict it reloads and applies the closure again, up
to 8 times), `set(value)`, `reload()`, `revision()`. The engine stores the documents (SQLite)
and the generator reads them.

`ctx.report().set(key, value)` writes a key of the session's results (`scenario.py results`);
it does not wait, and a failure shows up as a logic error.

## Documents for the web API

A logic publishes named JSON documents; the engine stores them and serves them read-only over
its HTTP API (`GET /api/v1/docs/<logic>/<name>`, a list at `/api/v1/docs`, a change stream at
`.../events`) for a site's live map or campaign page. API revision 3:
`#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 3)]`.

```rust
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct Front {
    sam_alive: usize,
    objective: [f64; 2], // lat, lon: the web API itself serves DCS metres only
}
// ctx.publish needs #[sortie::mission(api_rev = 3)]; ctx.dcs() is API revision 1.
let center = zones::OBJECTIVE.center().alt(m(0.0));
let (lat, lon, _alt) = ctx.dcs().coord().lo_to_ll(center).await?;
let sam_alive = ctx.world().group(&groups::SAM_NORTH).alive_count();
let front = Front {
    sam_alive,
    objective: [lat, lon],
};
let p = ctx.publish("front", &front).await?; // served at GET /api/v1/docs/<logic>/front
let _ = p.changed; // false: the engine had this JSON already (same `p.rev`)
let _removed = ctx.unpublish("old-front").await?; // false when there was none
```

- `ctx.publish(name, &value)` (`value: impl Serialize`, written with serde_json when called) ->
  `sortie::publish::Published { rev, updated_unix_ms, changed }`, once the engine stored it.
  The same JSON again changes nothing (`changed == false`, same `rev`): publishing on a timer
  is cheap. `ctx.unpublish(name)` -> `bool`, whether a document was removed.
- A document belongs to the logic (its `Attach.logic` name, the binary's name), not to the
  session: it outlives the session, the logic process and the engine (the state database).
  Publish when the data changes; there is nothing to restore at start.
- Rules, else `Error::Invalid` and nothing is stored: a name is 1 to 64 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9`,
  `_`, `-`; a document is at most 256 KiB of JSON; a logic has at most 64 documents; the
  logic's own name is 1 to 64 bytes of `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `-`.
- `rev` grows with every publish of any document of the engine and is never reused while the
  engine keeps its state database; an engine with its state in memory counts from 1 again
  after a restart. The HTTP `ETag` (and the stream's event id) is `<epoch>-<rev>`, where the
  epoch names the database: one ETag is one content, also across restarts.
- The web API serves points in DCS metres only: publish latitude and longitude yourself
  (`ctx.dcs().coord().lo_to_ll(point)`).
- A logic below revision 3 gets `Error::Revision`, an older engine `Error::EngineTooOld`;
  nothing is sent.
- HTTP callers never reach the logic or DCS; a site cannot change a document.

## Actions for the web API

A logic declares named actions; a site or a tool with an `operator` (or `admin`) token calls one
with `POST /api/v1/actions/<logic>/<name>` and a JSON body; the engine hands the request to the
logic, and the logic's answer is the HTTP response. The logic decides what happens in the game
(validate the body like any outside input). API revision 3: `#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 3)]`.

```rust
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Smoke {
    color: String, // "red" | "green"
}
#[derive(Serialize)]
struct Smoked {
    smoked: bool,
}
// ctx.api() needs #[sortie::mission(api_rev = 3)]. A site calls
// POST /api/v1/actions/<logic>/smoke_objective {"color": "red"} with an operator token.
let mut smoke = ctx.api().action("smoke_objective")?; // declared now, withdrawn on drop
ctx.spawn(async move |ctx| {
    while let Some(req) = smoke.next().await {
        let color = match req.json::<Smoke>() {
            Ok(s) if s.color == "red" => SmokeColor::Red,
            Ok(s) if s.color == "green" => SmokeColor::Green,
            Ok(_) => {
                req.fail(422, "color is red or green")?; // 4xx only
                continue;
            }
            Err(e) => {
                req.fail(400, e)?;
                continue;
            }
        };
        ctx.smoke(zones::OBJECTIVE.center(), color).await?;
        req.reply(&Smoked { smoked: true })?; // HTTP 200 {"smoked":true}; once per request
    }
    Ok(())
});
```

- `ctx.api().action(name)` -> `sortie::Result<sortie::api::ActionRequests>`: declares the
  action at once; `next().await` -> `Option<ActionRequest>`, `None` when the session ended.
  Dropping the stream or the end of the session withdraws the action; the mission function
  declares it again in the next session and after a restart of the logic process (until then
  callers get 503 `unavailable`).
- `ActionRequest`: `json::<T>()` (`Error::Invalid` whose text says what did not fit),
  `body()` (the JSON bytes; an empty body is `null`), `token()` (`Option<&str>`, the caller's
  token name), `role()` (`"operator"` or `"admin"`), `name()`.
- Answer once: `reply(&value)` -> 200 with that JSON (at most 1 MiB); `fail(status, message)`
  with a status 400..=499 -> `{"error": {"code": "refused", "message": ..}}`. Both consume the
  request and return `sortie::Result<()>` (`Error::Invalid` for a value that is not JSON, too
  large, or a status outside 4xx: the caller then gets 500). A request dropped unanswered
  (end of the loop, `?`, the session's end) is answered 500 `unanswered` by the SDK.
- The engine waits 10 s (`sortie::api::ACTION_TIMEOUT`), then answers 504 itself. Answer
  first and do long work afterwards (`ctx.spawn`), reporting progress in a published document.
  A 504 does not say whether the action ran: let the caller send an order id and key the
  commands with it (`.key(..)`), so a retried call does not run twice.
- Read the stream promptly: a request that waited 10 s in the queue is never handed to the
  logic (its caller got 504); the SDK answers it `unanswered` when the next one arrives or on
  `next()`.
- Rules, else `Error::Invalid` and nothing is declared: a name is 1 to 64 bytes of `a-z`,
  `0-9`, `_`, `-`; at most 64 actions; one stream per action at a time; the logic's own name is
  1 to 64 bytes of `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `-`. Below revision 3 `Error::Revision`, an
  older engine `Error::EngineTooOld`.
- The engine also refuses before the logic sees anything: another role (403), a body that is
  not JSON (400) or above `[http] max_body_bytes` (413), more than `[http] actions_per_s` calls
  of one token (429; counted per token, not per token name). `GET /api/v1/actions` lists what
  attached logics declare.

## DCS calls

`ctx.dcs()` reaches the DCS functions of the DCS API catalog (`catalog/dcs_api.toml` in the
SDK repository; the full list is `docs/dcs-catalog.md`) through generated, typed wrappers, for
what has no typed operation yet. The logic declares `#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 1)]`, else
every call is `Error::Revision` and nothing is sent.

```rust
#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 1)] // ctx.dcs() is API revision 1
pub async fn run(ctx: Ctx<Frontline>, _start: Start) -> sortie::Result<()> {
    let dcs = ctx.dcs();
    // Reads: no key (a key on a read is Error::Invalid).
    let surface = dcs.land().surface_type(zones::OBJECTIVE.center()).await?; // "ROAD"
    let sam: Vec<DcsObject> = dcs.group(groups::SAM_NORTH).units().await?;
    let fuel = dcs.unit(&sam[0]).fuel().await?;
    // Mutators: off until the engine owner enables them; always keyed.
    match dcs
        .sounds()
        .out_sound("l10n/DEFAULT/alarm.ogg")
        .key("alarm-1")
        .await
    {
        Ok(()) | Err(Error::Rejected(_)) => {} // Rejected: switched off in engine.toml
        Err(e) => return Err(e),
    }
    let lase: Handle = dcs
        .spots()
        .create_laser(
            &sam[0],
            None,
            zones::OBJECTIVE.center().alt(m(0)),
            Some(1688.0),
        )
        .key("lase-1")
        .await?;
    dcs.spot(lase).destroy().key("lase-1-off").await?;
    let _ = (surface, fuel);
    ctx.end_session(Outcome::Draw).await
}
```

- Families: `land()`, `atmosphere()`, `timer()`, `coord()`, `coalition()`, `world()`, `env()`,
  `effects()`, `sounds()`, `spots()`, `net()` and `server()` (hooks); methods of an object:
  `unit(u)`, `group(g)`, `static_object(o)`, `airbase(a)`, `warehouse(w)`, `controller(c)`,
  `spot(handle)`, `object(o)`. A target is a scenario symbol, an `Eid`, a `Group`, a world
  entity, a `sortie::sel` selector or a `DcsObject` an earlier call returned. Inherited methods
  (`point()`, `coalition()`) are in every class's family; a method runs through the class of
  its object, as `unit:getCoalition()` does (the catalog path `CoalitionObject.getCoalition`
  is the entry's name: DCS has no `CoalitionObject` table).
- Each catalog entry is a capability `call:<env>:<path>` (state, signature, live check):
  `ctx.capability(caps::call::mission::LAND_GET_HEIGHT)` finds one ("Capabilities" below).
- Hooks-environment calls (`net()`, `server()`) need a running mission session in this release
  (wave 1), like mission calls: without one they are `sortie::unavailable`.
- Results are typed: enum numbers as their key (`"ROAD"`), coalitions as `Coalition`, points as
  `Vec3` / `MapPoint`, objects as `DcsObject { class, eid, name, type_name, .. }`, spots as
  `Handle`, tables as `sortie::dcs::Value`. A number DCS returns as a string (ids in 2.9.31)
  is still an `f64` where the catalog says `number` (`static_object(o).id()`).
- Point arguments follow the catalog entry: `vec2` is a `MapPoint` (`land().height(p)`), `vec3`
  a `Vec3` in DCS axes, x north, y up, z east (`land().profile(a, b)`: DCS reads x and z).
- A warehouse item (`item_count`; the deprecated `add_item`, `remove_item`, `set_item`: change
  stock with `ctx.warehouse_op()`, "Warehouses") is its name
  (`"weapons.missiles.AIM_9"`) or its wsType, four whole numbers: `[4, 4, 7, 22]` or
  `(4, 4, 7, 22)` (`sortie::dcs::WarehouseItem`); MOOSE's `ENUMS.Storage` uses both forms.
  `inventory(Some(..))` takes a name only. FakeDcs keeps a wsType's stock apart from its name's.
- Reads (`read`, `heavy`) take no key: a key on a read is `Error::Invalid`. Mutators (`mutate`)
  are off until the engine owner enables them in `<Saved Games>/Sortie/engine.toml` (`[calls]
  enable = [..]`) or runs `sortied --dev`; until then `Error::Rejected` naming the capability
  `call:mission:<path>`. In `enable` and `disable` a method is named by its catalog entry, the
  class that defines it (`Object.destroy`, not `Unit.destroy`): the entry is one for every
  class, and an inherited name stops `sortied` at start. A mutator repeats its effect when run
  again: key it. A repeat with the same key does not reach DCS and returns the stored result,
  objects and handles included (a replayed `create_laser(..).key("lase-1")` gives the same
  `Handle`); only a result above 64 KiB is stored without its values, and its repeat is
  `Error::ResultNotKept`.
- The engine checks every call against the catalog: wrong arguments are `Error::Invalid` with
  the entry's signature, an argument out of the entry's range (explosion power above 5000) too.
  A sound file is a path inside the `.miz` (relative, no `..`). Guard `span_300km`: the two ends
  of `land().profile(..)`, `land().path_on_roads(..)` and `land().road_path(..)` lie at most
  300 km apart on the map, else `Error::Invalid` and nothing reaches DCS.
- Limits per writer (the logic's token name, else its name), refused at submit with
  `Error::Rejected` "rate limit: ..." and nothing sent. Counts: read 200/s, mutate 50/s, heavy
  2/s, admin 1/s (a batch takes all its calls; a 256-read batch leaves under 0.3 s of debt).
  DCS time (`cost_us`, the time a command took inside DCS's frame), charged when the result
  comes back, a late result after `Error::Timeout` too: reads and every batch, a batch with a
  mutate included, pay from `dcs_time.read` (20 ms a second, 20 ms at most; a read or batch
  that cost more refuses the writer's single reads for at most 1 s, its next batch until the
  whole debt is paid back); heavy calls pay from their own
  `dcs_time.heavy` (20 ms a second, 200 ms at most, the whole debt kept: after a heavy call of
  C ms the next heavy call waits about (C - 200) / 20 s, 102 s after a 2241 ms road path, and
  reads such as `timer().time()` pass at once). One heavy call of a writer at a time: the next
  one sent while the previous is not back is `Error::Rejected` (`DcsTime`, `dcs_time.heavy`, no
  `retry_after()`); send heavy calls one after the other, not in `join!`. The debt belongs to
  the writer: restarting the logic does not clear it. A single mutate call pays no DCS time.
- A big table comes back whole or as `Value::Cut(n)` (its key count) with `truncated` on the
  `Return`: deeper than `.max_depth(n)` (6 by default), after 50 000 table entries of one call,
  or when the answer of the whole command, every call of a batch together, would pass 150 000
  values (objects count with their description). A wrapper that expects a list then fails
  with `Error::Invalid`; split a big read into several commands.
- An object, id or name argument must be of the class the entry declares, also when it is a
  `Handle` or the result of an earlier call of a batch: a spot is no `object:Object`, a
  unit's id no group id. The wrong class is `Error::Invalid`, and DCS is not called with it.
- The world replica does not learn what a mutator changed until the next sweep (airbase owner:
  the next resync snapshot, then an `AirbaseOwnerChanged{Discovered}`; destroyed objects). Prefer the typed operation where one exists: such wrappers are
  `#[deprecated]` and name it (`ctx.smoke(..)` for `effects().smoke(..)`).
- The untyped call by path is behind the cargo feature `dcs-raw`:
  `ctx.dcs().call("land.getHeight").arg(sortie::dcs::arg::vec2(p))`, and `ctx.dcs().batch()`.
- An engine owner's entry (`engine.toml` `[[calls.call]]`) is called by path. Its `enum:<table>`
  type names the whole path of a published DCS table: 2 to 6 Lua names from an enum root (`AI`,
  `Airbase`, `Controller`, `Group`, `Object`, `Spot`, `StaticObject`, `Unit`, `Weapon`,
  `coalition`, `country`, `land`, `radio`, `trigger`, `world`), so
  `enum:AI.Option.Ground.val.ALARM_STATE` loads (0.3.0 refused 5 names); a data root (`env`,
  `net`, `DCS`, `timer`) or 7 names stops `sortied` at start. Pass a key,
  `arg::enum_key("AI.Option.Ground.val.ALARM_STATE", "RED")` (the layer reads the running DCS's
  number), or (0.4.0) one of the table's numbers, `arg::number(2.0)`, which the layer checks is a
  value of the table (`Error::Invalid` otherwise; a layer before 0.4.0 refuses numbers there).
  Alarm states and ROE have the typed `group.set_option(..)`, which needs no owner entry.

### A road path

`ctx.dcs().land().path_on_roads(..)` asks DCS for a path along roads between two map points
(`land.findPathOnRoads`). It is API revision 3: `#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 3)]`, else
`Error::Revision`; an engine of an older revision is `Error::EngineTooOld`.

```rust
#[sortie::mission(api_rev = 3)] // the road path is API revision 3
pub async fn convoy_distance(ctx: Ctx<Frontline>, _start: Start) -> sortie::Result<()> {
    let armor = ctx.group(groups::RED_ARMOR)?;
    let objective = zones::OBJECTIVE.center();
    let Some(here) = ctx.world().group(&armor).center() else {
        return ctx.end_session(Outcome::Draw).await;
    };
    // Road type, then x (north) and y (east) of the start and of the end.
    let points = ctx
        .dcs()
        .land()
        .path_on_roads(
            "roads",
            here.north,
            here.east,
            objective.north,
            objective.east,
        )
        .await?; // Option<Vec<MapPoint>>, start to end; None: DCS answered nil
    // The length along the points; None (null in the report) when DCS found no path.
    let km: Option<f64> =
        points.map(|p| p.windows(2).map(|w| w[0].distance(w[1])).sum::<f64>() / 1000.0);
    ctx.report().set("road_km_to_objective", km);
    ctx.end_session(Outcome::Draw).await
}
```

- Arguments as DCS takes them: the road type, then x (north) and y (east) of the start and of
  the end, in map metres (`MapPoint.north` / `.east`).
- Road type `"roads"`. For railroads the Hoggit wiki documents `"railroads"` and reports that
  DCS reads `"rails"`; which one works is not measured yet.
- The answer is `Option<Vec<MapPoint>>`, start to end. `None` is DCS's nil (the Mission
  Editor reads nil as "no path found"). What DCS returns for a point no road reaches (nil, an
